A clearer picture of cyclone wind risk
for Bangladesh
A track shows where a cyclone may
travel
But which communities face damaging winds
How many people could be exposed
And how uncertain is the answer
Ghurni starts with real archived ensemble forecasts
Each line is one possible storm path
This Remal replay uses forecasts issued before
landfall
rather than pretending we already knew the
outcome
Compare forecasts around seventy-two
forty-eight and twenty-four hours before landfall
Watch the estimated impacts change
Ghurni keeps those changes visible rather than
showing one certain answer
Each member passes through a physics-based wind
model
Local boundaries and population estimates connect winds
to communities
producing wind-threshold probabilities
and a range of possible population exposure
Explore five thousand
one hundred and sixty unions
Search a place inspect wind probabilities and
compare forecast cycles
These are estimates of population exposure not
casualty predictions
Adjustable probability rules create Act Prepare and
Monitor lists
The threshold stays visible and priorities can
be exported
These are planning rules for review
not evacuation instructions
A template briefing combines forecasts and priorities
for human review
Change the forecast or decision rule
and approval resets
Nothing is sent automatically
Controls explanations and exports work in Bangla
and English
The map keeps geography central
Its dated Sentinel-two satellite mosaic provides context
not live storm imagery
Evidence compares six historical storms against a
single-forecast baseline
Reference impacts use observed tracks and the
same wind model
This limited backtest is not independent validation
against measured damage
Ghurni is a historical wind-risk prototype
Numerical forecasts and physical modelling support preparedness
analysis
Always follow official Bangladesh Meteorological Department warnings
